title: Idempotent fastpath & edge retry dampener for hosted API escalations
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: During the last two customer escalations we observed large tenant-visible latency and a wave of 5xxs driven by a combination of edge TLS renegotiation storms, client SDK aggressive retry loops, and our in-flight KV cache compaction leaving short-lived connection spikes. Multiple customers reported repeated failures even after backend recovery because their SDKs retried on ambiguous errors and created an amplification loop.

Scope: This ticket implements a mitigation that (1) establishes a safe idempotent fastpath for high-priority tenants and verified idempotent requests, (2) introduces an edge-side retry dampener that coordinates with the SDKs via a short-lived server-provided cooling token, (3) adds telemetry to correlate retries to originating request ids and connection lifecycles, and (4) provides a staged rollout and communication plan for affected customers. This is a platform-side mitigation — it does not require immediate SDK updates but provides an interoperable token that SDKs can adopt later for reduced client-side retries.

Proposal:
- Idempotent fastpath: Accept X-Idempotency-Token on generation and embedding routes; where present and verified (signature match + not-seen), mark the request eligible for priority fastpath admission that bypasses non-essential fanout layers and uses a limited dedicated pool.
- Edge retry dampener: On server-side detection of elevated retry amplification (per-tenant rolling window), issue a short-lived Retry-Cooling-Token in responses and a Retry-Delay header. Edge proxies will honor the token by returning 429 with a Retry-After when they see repeated identical inbound idempotency tokens within the cooling window.
- Adaptive admission: Per-tenant admission controller that reduces new in-flight for noisy tenants and preserves small reserved fastpath capacity for verified idempotent requests.
- Observability: New trace tag retry.amplification=true and link all retries to original request id. Export a daily report showing per-tenant retry factor and edge-triggered 5xx correlation.
- Rollout: Canary to 3 low-risk tenants, then expand to tiered rollout with telemetry thresholds.

Risks and tradeoffs:
- Introducing idempotency semantics on generation endpoints may change semantics for callers that rely on non-idempotent behavior; mitigation: opt-in via header and explicit docs + knob to turn off per-tenant.
- Edge-side 429s will surface to customers not upgrading SDKs; mitigate by returning clear guidance and the Retry-Cooling-Token so SDKs can implement backoff logic without additional server roundtrips.

Operational runbook (high level):
1) Detect amplification: dashboards alert when per-tenant retry factor > 10x baseline and 5xx rate increases by 3x in 2m.
2) Automatic damping: edge starts returning soft 429s with Retry-Cooling-Token for identical tokens.
3) Human recovery: SRE paginates, adjust admission controller thresholds and communicate to Customer Success.

Deliverables: implementation PRs for edge proxy, admission controller, runtime admission fastpath, tracing additions, Confluence runbook, and customer-facing KB article.
acceptance_criteria: Edge returns Retry-Cooling-Token and Retry-After when retry amplification is detected for identical idempotency tokens
Verified idempotent requests gain admission to the reserved fastpath and bypass non-essential fanout within SLA targets
Per-tenant retry factor telemetry is emitted and visible in console dashboard with ability to filter by trace id
Canary rollout to 3 tenants shows reduced 5xx delta vs control group (target >= 40% reduction in retry-related 5xx)
Confluence runbook drafted and SRE sign-off complete
KB and customer comms template prepared for Customer Success
notes: We intentionally make fastpath opt-in to avoid changing existing caller semantics. The plan integrates with runtime admission tokens and uses the existing token signing service (work tracked in ENG-271828).
